# Biology Lab

> Free biology virtual labs, calculators and interactive tools for students and teachers: Punnett squares, DNA to mRNA to protein, population growth, cell size, enzyme kinetics and a 3D cell, with concept notes, practice questions, printable worksheets and teacher answer keys. Everything runs in the browser with no account. From the makers of Interactive Periodic Table.

## Tools

- [DNA to mRNA to Protein Converter: Transcription & Translation](https://thebiologylab.org/dna-transcription-translation/): Free transcription and translation tool: paste DNA or mRNA to get mRNA, tRNA anticodons and amino acids, or the complementary strand in DNA replication.
- [Hardy-Weinberg Calculator — Allele & Genotype Frequencies](https://thebiologylab.org/hardy-weinberg-calculator/): Find allele frequencies p and q and genotype frequencies p², 2pq, q² from p, a recessive phenotype frequency, or genotype counts, then test equilibrium with χ².
- [Population Growth Calculator: Solve Growth & Doubling Problems](https://thebiologylab.org/population-growth-calculator/): Solve population growth word problems step by step: the population after t years at a % rate, the years to reach a target, and doubling-time problems.
- [Punnett Square Calculator: Genotype & Phenotype Ratios](https://thebiologylab.org/punnett-square-calculator/): Free Punnett square calculator for monohybrid (2x2), dihybrid (4x4), and ABO blood type crosses: genotype and phenotype ratios, probabilities, and steps.
- [Biology Calculators & Virtual Labs: All Free Tools](https://thebiologylab.org/tools/): Every free biology calculator and virtual lab in one list: Punnett squares, DNA to mRNA, Hardy-Weinberg, population growth, SA:V ratio and water potential.
- [3D Animal and Plant Cell Model: Interactive Organelles](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/3d/): Turn a 3D animal and plant cell, pull it apart to watch each organelle float out with its label, and tap the nucleus or a chloroplast to learn what it does.
- [Label the Cell: Animal and Plant Cell Diagram Quiz](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/label-the-cell/): Label a numbered animal or plant cell diagram from a word bank or by typing, get instant feedback and a score, then match each organelle to its function.
- [Bacterial Doubling Time Calculator: Generation Time & Growth](https://thebiologylab.org/tools/bacterial-growth/): Find bacterial generation (doubling) time from two counts, or the cells after any time with N = N₀ × 2ⁿ, and see exponential growth on a log-scale curve.
- [Surface Area to Volume Ratio Calculator for Cells (SA:V)](https://thebiologylab.org/tools/cell-size/): Calculate the surface area, volume and surface area to volume ratio (SA:V) of a cube-shaped or spherical cell from its side length or radius, with steps.
- [Chi-Square Test Calculator for Genetics: χ², df & p-Value](https://thebiologylab.org/tools/chi-square-test/): Test whether observed offspring counts fit a 3:1, 1:1, 1:2:1 or 9:3:3:1 Mendelian ratio: χ², degrees of freedom, critical value, p-value and verdict.
- [Dilution Calculator (C1V1 = C2V2) — Stock, Final & Serial](https://thebiologylab.org/tools/dilution-calculator/): Solve C₁V₁ = C₂V₂ for the stock volume or final concentration, get the diluent to add, and plan serial dilutions with the concentration after every step.
- [Energy Pyramid Calculator — The 10% Rule Across Trophic Levels](https://thebiologylab.org/tools/energy-pyramid/): Enter the energy captured by producers and a transfer efficiency to see how much reaches each consumer level, how much is lost, and why food chains stay short.
- [Michaelis-Menten Calculator: Enzyme Kinetics, Vmax & Km](https://thebiologylab.org/tools/enzyme-kinetics/): Michaelis-Menten calculator: find the reaction rate from Vmax, Km and substrate concentration, then add a competitive or noncompetitive inhibitor.
- [Magnification Calculator — Actual Size, Image Size & Scale Bar](https://thebiologylab.org/tools/magnification-calculator/): Find actual size, image size, or magnification with correct mm-to-µm conversion, work out total microscope magnification, and size a scale bar.
- [Predator–Prey Simulator — Lotka–Volterra Population Cycles](https://thebiologylab.org/tools/predator-prey/): Simulate prey and predator populations with the Lotka–Volterra equations: set the four rates, watch the boom-and-bust cycles, and find the equilibrium point.
- [Water Potential Calculator: Solute Potential Ψs = −iCRT](https://thebiologylab.org/tools/water-potential/): Calculate solute potential with Ψs = −iCRT and water potential Ψ = Ψs + Ψp in MPa or bars, then compare two cells to see which way water moves by osmosis.

- [Hardy-Weinberg Principle: What p and q Mean, With Example](https://thebiologylab.org/learn/hardy-weinberg-principle/): The baseline of a population that isn’t evolving. For a gene with two alleles, let p be the frequency of the dominant allele A and q the frequency of the…
- [Lab measurements & scale — Key Idea & Worked Example](https://thebiologylab.org/learn/lab-measurements/): Turn what you see in a microscope into numbers. Magnification is image size divided by actual size (rearranged: image = actual × magnification), and it only…

- [Mitosis & meiosis — Key Idea & Worked Example](https://thebiologylab.org/learn/mitosis-and-meiosis/): Copy a cell, or halve its chromosome set. Both divisions follow an interphase in which DNA is replicated (S phase), so each chromosome enters division…
- [Natural selection — Key Idea & Worked Example](https://thebiologylab.org/learn/natural-selection/): Variation, heredity, and who leaves more offspring. Darwin’s mechanism needs three ingredients: individuals in a population vary (thanks to mutation and the…
- [Photosynthesis — Key Idea & Worked Example](https://thebiologylab.org/learn/photosynthesis/): Light, water, and CO₂ become sugar and oxygen. In the light-dependent reactions, chlorophyll in the thylakoid membranes absorbs light; photosystem II splits…
- [Exponential vs Logistic Population Growth Models Explained](https://thebiologylab.org/learn/population-growth/): Exponential with no limits, logistic with them. When resources are unlimited a population grows exponentially: the per-capita growth rate r (births minus…
- [Prokaryotes vs. eukaryotes — Key Idea & Worked Example](https://thebiologylab.org/learn/prokaryotes-vs-eukaryotes/): Two cell plans: one with a nucleus, one without. Prokaryotes (bacteria and archaea) are typically 1–10 µm across and keep a single circular chromosome in a…

## Reference

- [Cell Organelles and Their Functions: Labeled Diagram & Chart](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/): A labeled animal and plant cell diagram plus a chart of cell organelles and their functions, from the nucleus and mitochondria to ribosomes, ER, and Golgi.
- [Codon Chart & Codon Table: All 64 mRNA Codons to Amino Acids](https://thebiologylab.org/codon-chart/): Codon chart and codon table of the genetic code: all 64 mRNA codons with their amino acids, the DNA codons, the start and stop codons, and a codon lookup.
- [Cell membrane: Structure and Function in the Cell](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/cell-membrane/): The cell membrane, or plasma membrane, is a phospholipid bilayer about 7–8 nm thick that separates a cell from its surroundings. Structure and function.
- [Chloroplast: Structure and Function in the Cell](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/chloroplast/): Chloroplasts capture light energy and use it to build sugar from carbon dioxide and water. Structure, functions, size, and a common misconception.
- [Endoplasmic reticulum: Structure and Function in the Cell](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/endoplasmic-reticulum/): The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a maze of membrane tubes and sacs continuous with the nuclear envelope. Structure, functions, and a common misconception.
- [Golgi apparatus: Structure and Function in the Cell](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/golgi-apparatus/): The Golgi apparatus receives proteins and lipids from the ER, finishes them, and sorts them into vesicles for delivery. Structure and function.
- [Lysosome: Structure and Function in the Cell](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/lysosome/): Lysosomes are acidic sacs of enzymes that digest worn-out organelles, engulfed microbes, and large molecules. Structure, functions, and a common misconception.
- [Mitochondria (Mitochondrion): Structure and Function](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/mitochondrion/): Mitochondria run aerobic respiration, converting the energy in glucose and fats into ATP the cell can spend. Structure, functions, and a common misconception.
- [Nucleus: Structure and Function in the Cell](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/nucleus/): The nucleus stores the cell’s DNA and decides which genes are read at any moment. Structure, functions, size, and a common misconception.
- [Ribosome: Structure and Function in the Cell](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/ribosome/): Ribosomes read messenger RNA three bases at a time and link amino acids into proteins. Structure, functions, size, and a common misconception.

## Classroom

- [Biology Practice Questions: 100 Free Questions with Answers](https://thebiologylab.org/practice/): 100 free biology practice questions with answers and explanations: cells, genetics, molecular biology, ecology and human physiology, in rounds of eight.
- [Printable Cell Diagrams & Punnett Square Worksheets (PDF/SVG)](https://thebiologylab.org/printable-diagrams/): Free printable animal and plant cell diagrams to label, blank monohybrid and dihybrid Punnett square grids, and a pedigree chart, each with an answer key.
- [Biology Lab for Teachers: Free Activities with Answer Keys](https://thebiologylab.org/teachers/): Free biology virtual labs and calculators with 12 printable classroom activities, answer keys and NGSS connections. No logins; works on Chromebooks.
- [Biology Worksheets (PDF): Free Printables with Answer Keys](https://thebiologylab.org/worksheets/): Free printable biology worksheets with answer keys: pick cells, genetics, molecular biology, ecology or physiology and 8, 12 or 20 questions. Save as PDF.
